topic: Eddie Tipton, the lottery security director who secretly rigged jackpots he was paid to protect
title: The Lottery Security Chief Who Secretly Rigged His Own Jackpots
description: AI-narrated commentary on the real story of Eddie Tipton, the lottery security director convicted of secretly rigging multi-state jackpots. Independent sources are linked below.

hook_candidates.text: **Eddie Tipton's** job was protecting the lottery's random numbers. Nobody protected the lottery from him.
What if the person guarding the lottery's random numbers was the one secretly rigging them?
People assume lottery fraud needs an outside hacker. The biggest one was run by the lottery's own security chief.
In 2010, a man in a hoodie tried to claim a $16.5 million jackpot no one could trace to him.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists apps and lottery drawings can't be secretly rigged, because they want to prove an insider pulled it off for years.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume the lottery's random numbers can't be secretly controlled by the very person protecting them.
closing_comment: The wildest part is that his own coworker's ear caught what years of lottery security never did.

sources.note: Confirms Tipton, the ex-lottery security official, pleaded guilty and was sentenced for rigging jackpots in multiple states.
Confirms he installed a rootkit on the RNG computer that let him predict winning numbers on set days.
Confirms Tipton was later granted parole after serving time for the multi-state lottery rigging scheme.
